## Mobile surveillance in Baltimore

Baltimore is our home market. VDS has been headquartered in Pikesville since 2017, and our staging yard is 15 minutes from the Inner Harbor, 20 minutes from the Port of Baltimore, and 25 minutes from BWI. We've run more deployments in the Baltimore metro than in any other city — and most of our same-day deployment capacity in the country routes through this hub.

The Baltimore market mix is industrial-heavy: Port of Baltimore container and roll-on/roll-off terminals, BWI cargo and construction, Inner Harbor mixed-use development, Johns Hopkins medical and East Baltimore campus expansion, and the Tradepoint Atlantic redevelopment at Sparrows Point. That's before counting the auto dealer corridor on Pulaski Highway and the parking-lot density of downtown.

## Industries we protect in Baltimore metro

- **Construction.** Mixed-use, infrastructure, medical campus, residential mid-rise.
- **Port and logistics.** Container terminals, vehicle processing, intermodal yards.
- **Auto dealers.** Pulaski Highway corridor, Reisterstown Road, White Marsh.
- **Parking and transit lots.** Downtown garages, MARC station lots, MTA park-and-rides.
- **Municipal and government.** Baltimore County and City Public Works yards, MDOT.

## Coverage and lead time

We cover Baltimore City, Baltimore County, Anne Arundel, Howard, Harford, and Carroll counties from the Pikesville yard. Same-day deployment is available for most of Baltimore City and inner Baltimore County. Next-business-day for the rest of the metro. We also stage units at BWI cargo-side for jobs at the airport and along the I-95 corridor.

Lead time from quote-signed to power-on, average, in the Baltimore metro: 6 hours.

## A Baltimore-area deployment

A downtown high-rise general contractor signed a Mobile Surveillance Unit at $2,200/mo for a 26-month mixed-use project near the Inner Harbor after their previous vendor's cellular-only unit went offline during a copper theft incident. We deployed within 4 hours of contract sign — same morning — and the SOC handled 38 escalations in the first 90 days. False-alarm rate post-tuning: under 3%. The GC has since added two units across other Baltimore-area projects.

## Local compliance note

Baltimore City has no specific ordinance restricting private mobile surveillance on private property, but several construction zones along the Inner Harbor and around Johns Hopkins are inside Baltimore City Right-of-Way permit jurisdiction. If a unit sits on a sidewalk or shoulder, we pull the ROW permit and post signage per Baltimore DOT rules.

Maryland's wiretap statute (Md. Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 10-402) is two-party-consent for audio. Our units capture video only by default; audio is disabled unless the customer has documented all-party consent.

The Port of Baltimore requires TWIC-credentialed escorts and MTSA-compliant access on the secure side of terminal fencing. We've run jobs at Seagirt and Dundalk Marine Terminal and our deployment crew is current on the credentialing.

## Mobile surveillance in Chicago

Chicago is the largest inland rail hub in the United States — every Class I freight railroad meets here — and one of the highest-volume retail and ORC enforcement markets in the country. The Mag Mile retail corridor, the CTA and Metra transit construction programs, the data center build-out tied to CME Group and the financial market infrastructure, and the broader Chicagoland industrial and logistics market drive most of our deployment volume here.

Chicagoland is also the most aggressive biometric privacy environment in the US. The Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA) has produced more private-litigation risk for surveillance vendors than any other state statute. To be direct: **VDS does not collect, store, or process biometric information. We do not run facial recognition. We do not run iris, voice, gait, or any other biometric matching.** This is a configuration default, not a feature we toggle off on request.

## Industries we protect in the Chicago metro

- **Construction.** Downtown high-rise, West Loop, Fulton Market, suburban mixed-use.
- **Transit and infrastructure.** CTA station and yard construction, Metra facility upgrades, IDOT projects.
- **Logistics and rail.** Inland intermodal yards, distribution-center perimeter, last-mile facilities.
- **Retail and ORC.** Mag Mile, downtown flagship retail, and flash-mob-targeted locations.
- **Data centers.** Northern Chicagoland data center construction corridor.

## Coverage and lead time

We cover Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake (IL), McHenry, and Will counties from a Chicagoland staging hub. Lead time: 2–4 business days from contract sign to power-on for most Chicago-metro deployments. Mag Mile and downtown placements with Chicago DOT ROW permits add 5–7 business days for permit issuance.

## A Chicago-area deployment

A Mag Mile retail loss-prevention director signed three Mobile Surveillance Unit units ($4,500/mo combined) for flash-mob and after-hours coverage of two flagship locations during a stretch of organized retail theft incidents. Deployment power-on time: under 36 hours from contract sign. SOC handled 21 escalations in the first 90 days, including a documented flash-mob attempt that dispersed when CPD responded to a verified SOC dispatch. The retailer added a fourth unit two months later.

## Local compliance note

**Illinois BIPA.** No biometric data is collected, stored, or processed in any VDS deployment. No facial recognition, no iris, no voice print, no gait analysis. This is a stack-level configuration default — the capability is not installed.

**Chicago surveillance disclosure.** Chicago has no enacted POST Act equivalent today, but we structure private-property contracts with the same private-property-only framing we use in NYC. Customer-owned footage, audit-trail logging, and explicit law-enforcement-access-by-subpoena terms in every contract.

**Illinois wiretap law.** Illinois is two-party consent for audio (720 ILCS 5/14-2). Video only by default; audio disabled unless customer documents all-party consent.

**Chicago DOT permits.** Right-of-way placement in the City of Chicago requires a CDOT permit. We file on the customer's behalf. Typical issuance: 5–7 business days.

**Rail and intermodal access.** Class I railroad intermodal yard access requires railroad-specific credentialing. Our crew is current on the major operators serving the Chicagoland hub.
